name: Jack Friks
tagline: Solo founder of Post Bridge; grows apps with organic short-form video

quote.text: if you can't do it manually, there's no point of automating it because you're not going to know what works and what doesn't.

topics.label: Organic TikTok and Instagram growth
topics.summary: Fresh niche accounts, warm-up, one manual post a day, CTA in caption and pinned comment, no ad spend.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I get my first 1,000 app downloads from TikTok without paying for ads?

topics.label: Copying and milking proven formats
topics.summary: Scroll your niche, save what went viral, recreate it, and repeat a winning format until results stop.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I find a video format that actually converts for my app?

topics.label: Building for your own problems
topics.summary: Pick ideas from your own problems, keep products lean, and compete in crowded markets on fair price.
topics.sampleQuestion: Is it fine to build a product in a market with hundreds of competitors?

topics.label: Paywalls and onboarding
topics.summary: Hard paywalls with trials, onboarding that sells results first, and when he switched an app to freemium.
topics.sampleQuestion: Should my consumer app use a hard paywall or freemium?

topics.label: Shipping apps with AI coding
topics.summary: Went from not coding to multiple apps using ChatGPT, Cursor and Claude; tips on docs, models, security.
topics.sampleQuestion: Can I ship a mobile app with AI tools if I can't code?

topics.label: Staying solo, profitable and consistent
topics.summary: Profitability over scale, daily reps, a public record of misses, and turning down a $1M offer.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I keep going when my app has made almost nothing for months?

principles.text: Make a fresh account per app, warm it up by scrolling only your niche, then post about one video a day by hand.
Recreate formats that already went viral in your niche, and keep reusing a winner until results actually stop.
Never make the video an ad. Give value first and put the call to action in the caption and pinned comment.
Build tools that solve your own problems; it is the easiest way to make a successful business.
Marketing is most of the work. A good app with no distribution gets no downloads or money.

sampleQA.question: How do I get my first downloads for a new app without ads?

answer.text: Make a brand new account for the app and warm it up for a few days to a week, only engaging with content in your niche so the algorithm learns your audience.
Post manually, about one video every 24 hours. Posting fast on a new account often gets zero views.
Recreate formats that already went viral in your niche and put the download CTA in the caption and pinned comment.
Judge formats by downloads, not views, and expect around 30 videos before one does well.

sampleQA.question: Hard paywall or freemium for a consumer app?

answer.text: His default is a hard paywall with a 7-day free trial, which he says converts much better than freemium.
Sell results in a longer onboarding before the paywall. Remove trials first to measure true conversion, then A/B test them back in.
Exception: he moved his couples app to freemium so a partner could use it without a credit card, which helps ratings and word of mouth.

sampleQA.question: Should I build something that already has lots of competitors?

answer.text: Yes. He built a social media scheduler in 2024 when there were already 1,000 of them, and it makes about $20k/month.
Don't fight on feature comparisons. Offer real value at a fair price and let pricing, features and word of mouth do the work.
He builds in niches where a successful counterpart already exists and borrows what works in its marketing.
